notes: Measured on one isolated gateway with a snapshot of 67 real farm runs. A pending gate uses an isolated repository and slot; unavailable legacy artifact references were removed from that gate fixture.

Run list means the inventory window on Command Center and the first active-run reply on Companion, matching current client bootstrap behavior. Raw observations record row counts and the earlier first reply where present.

Times end at the successful read reply; browser gate observations additionally include renderedMs and a check of the displayed diff. Bytes count received UTF-8 websocket application frames, excluding framing and HTTP artifact traffic.
Command Center gate reads the committed branch file diff. Companion currently reads its live workspace diff; the isolated fixture includes a working-tree change for that path.
Remote HTTP is served by another machine through an SSH tunnel at an insecure test origin. The desktop uses its bundled production assets.

postMigrationMeasurements.head: 8bb523f4d644917acb964b052de085f127a3b0c7
notes: Gate open timing runs from navigation to the rendered diff table (CDP monotonic). Bytes are received gateway application frames plus /api/run-artifact HTTP transfer bytes (encodedDataLength); the earlier baseline counted frames only.

Each sample is a new document. nothingHeld is a second visible window with memory storage; afterPrefetch is the owner tab after its prefetch pass; offlineHeld is the owner tab with the gateway stopped.

A connected gate open reads its file diff with git.diff (method git.diff) or shows it from held content (method local); the package diff travels over /api/run-artifact only in prefetch or when held content and the live slot diff are both unavailable. The HTTP bytes on a connected open are other package files.
Fixture: one isolated gateway, one pending ready gate on a real package and three active runs, not the 67-run baseline snapshot; raw figures only, no normalized speedup claim.
Fix-loop figures are the gate prefetch reads after a new package for the same gate: requests, their replies and HTTP artifact bytes; held bases answer "held" and the over-cap base "too-large".
